Priya K.: Hey team, prepping answers for EnterpriseCorp's security questionnaire. They're asking for tenant-level KMS usage proofs + RBAC change history. Can we list exactly what artifacts we can provide and the safe redaction options?
Jordan H.: We can provide tenant-scoped audit logs (key usage, key rotation events), an exported signed manifest, and role binding snapshots.
Alex M.: +1. Also include service-account audit (who assumed what) and any policy change diffs. They usually want tamper-evidence, so signed manifests matter.
Sam R.: Quick Q: do we include raw key material fingerprints? we should avoid any private key exports.
Priya K.: No raw key material. Provide key IDs and KMS operation records (Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign) with timestamps and request IDs. If needed, we can include KMS HSM attestation statements (customer-facing) from the provider.
Maria L.: For RBAC, we can produce role_binding snapshots at requested time boundaries and a delta series for the last 90 days. We have an internal tool that exports this as ndjson. Example command:
```
redwood export rbac --tenant enterprisecorp --since 2024-01-01 --format ndjson > enterprisecorp-rbac.ndjson
redwood audit export --tenant enterprisecorp --from 2024-02-01 --to 2024-02-28 --format ndjson > enterprisecorp-audit.ndjson
```
Jordan H.: Nice. Also include a short README in the bundle that explains field mappings and hash markers for each file. Example manifest skeleton:
```
{
  "bundle_id": "bndl-20240228-ec",
  "files": ["enterprisecorp-audit.ndjson","enterprisecorp-rbac.ndjson"],
  "sha256": {"enterprisecorp-audit.ndjson": "<sha256>"}
}
```
sec-bot: Automated: evidence bundle builder available at /run/evidence/bundles. Use `sec-bot build-bundle --tenant enterprisecorp --window 30d` to create signed bundle.
Sam R.: On redaction: we can redact user email addresses and IPs on request, but must keep pseudonymous IDs + request IDs so they can audit sequences. Redaction policy should be explicit in README.
Priya K.: Customer asked about real-time log streaming vs. snapshot. We support both: snapshot exports for compliance packages and syslog/S3 streaming for SIEM ingest. Which do they prefer?
Alex M.: Ask them to confirm ingestion method. For SIEM we can configure a per-tenant syslog endpoint or S3 layout with signed presigned URLs. Note: streaming requires an SLA caveat for retention window.
Maria L.: Incident response proof question: they want traceability for a suspected misuse window. We can provide indexed events and a timeline we can generate from request IDs. Example event sample (ndjson line):
```
{ "ts": "2024-02-14T21:12:03Z", "event":"KMS.Encrypt", "key_id":"km-abc123", "request_id":"req-7a8b9c", "actor":"svc-app-42" }
```
Jordan H.: For attestation: we can sign the manifest with our internal signing key and include a notarization statement. Legal may want the signature chain; loop in @legal for details.
Priya K.: Action items: 1) Jordan create sample bundle + README, 2) Maria produce RBAC delta tooling output for last 90 days, 3) Alex draft a short note on streaming vs snapshot options and retention limits, 4) Sam draft redaction policy snippet. I'll assemble answers in the SQ template and flag open items for legal.
Alex M.: I'll also note fallback options if audit logs are incomplete (e.g., attestations + cache snapshots + cross-service correlators).
Sam R.: ETA for artifacts? can we target EOD Wednesday?
Jordan H.: EOD Wednesday works for sample bundle. Will attach example SHA manifests and a short verification script.
Maria L.: RBAC deltas ready by Tuesday morning.
Priya K.: Thanks all. tagging @legal and @solutions-eng for visibility. If EnterpriseCorp requests HSM-level certs, we'll coordinate with cloud provider and legal. :thumbsup:
